findings.title: parameterRanges typed Partial, forcing ! assertions and a dead no-clamp branch
findings.description: `parameterRanges` is declared `Readonly<Partial<Record<TargetParameterKey, …>>>` although the literal has all 10 keys. That forces `parameterRanges[key]!` in `randomizePlayerStart()` and a `range ? clamp : value` ternary in `decodeTargetParameters()` whose unclamped branch is unreachable today. If a key is ever added without a range, the compiler stays silent: the random start would produce `NaN` sliders and decoding would stop clamping that key, quietly reopening the hole #12 closes.

A.approach: Type it as `Readonly<Record<TargetParameterKey, readonly [number, number]>>`; drop both `!` and the ternary so the clamp always runs.
A.rationale: The compiler then requires a range for every key; no runtime change today.

B.approach: Keep `Partial` but throw when a range is missing instead of falling back to the unclamped value.
B.rationale: Fails loudly at runtime, but later than A and keeps the `!` pattern.

C.rationale: Correct today; relies on whoever adds a parameter remembering the range.

findings.title: Parameter key lists overlap across three static structures
findings.description: `targetParameterKeys`, `parameterRanges` and `playerParameterKeys` each enumerate overlapping key sets, so adding or removing a parameter touches up to three places.

A.approach: Derive one list from another (e.g. `targetParameterKeys` from `Object.keys(parameterRanges)`).
A.rationale: Single source of truth, but ties the link's wire order to object key order.

B.approach: Add a comment above each list pointing at the others.
B.rationale: Documents the coupling; relies on discipline.

C.approach: No change: with M1-A, a key missing from `parameterRanges` is a compile error, and `targetParameterKeys` must stay an explicit ordered list because its order is the shared link format.
C.rationale: M1-A removes the drift risk the finding describes; deriving would make the link format depend on object key order.

findings.title: `src/util` import differs from the file's relative imports
findings.description: `import { random } from 'src/util'` is baseUrl-rooted while the other imports in this file are relative.

B.rationale: Every existing importer of util (`shell-parameters.ts`, `shell-viewer.ts`) uses `"src/util"`, so this matches the codebase convention for that module.

C.approach: Switch all three util imports to relative paths.
C.rationale: Uniform, but touches files outside this PR's scope.

findings.title: Plan names `randomWithGenerator`; the code uses `random`
findings.description: plan.md says the random start reuses `randomWithGenerator(min, max, Math.random)`; `game.component.ts` imports `random` from `src/util` and calls `random(min, max)`. A reader tracing plan to code won't find the named call.

A.approach: Update both mentions to `random(min, max)` from `src/util.ts`, on the issue's plan comment and the cached plan.md.
A.rationale: Restores plan-to-code traceability; the issue comment is authoritative, so both change together.

B.approach: Leave it as a point-in-time design record.
B.rationale: Plans may diverge, but this archive is presented as the technical record.

C.approach: Add a short "as implemented" note under Research Findings.
C.rationale: Keeps the original text and records the delta.

findings.title: Plan's `?target` clearing call doesn't match the implementation
findings.description: plan.md describes `router.navigate([], { relativeTo: route, queryParams: {} })`, which would drop every query param and says nothing about history. The code uses `queryParams: { target: null }`, `queryParamsHandling: 'merge'` and `replaceUrl: true`; the last one is why Back and reload don't restore the challenge.

A.approach: Rewrite the bullet to describe `{ target: null }` + `merge` + `replaceUrl: true`, on the issue's plan comment and the cached plan.md.
A.rationale: Matches what ships, including the detail that makes the fix reload-proof.

B.rationale: Point-in-time record; misleads a reviewer checking the approach.

C.approach: Add a one-line "refined during implementation" note.

findings.title: Spec's "Clamp link values" omits pinning `d` to 1 (commit 354bb6e)
findings.description: Commit 354bb6e pins `d` (coiling direction, no slider) to 1 when decoding, so an edited link can't mirror the target. The spec's Proposed Fix doesn't mention `d`, while the PR description does.

A.approach: Add a sentence to "Clamp link values" that `d` is pinned to 1, on the issue's spec comment and the cached spec.md.
A.rationale: Keeps the authoritative spec complete and in line with the code and PR description.

B.approach: Leave it; the pinning came after the spec was written.
B.rationale: Expected staleness, but the spec is the acceptance record.

C.approach: Add an addendum at the end of the spec referencing 354bb6e.
C.rationale: Records the delta without editing the original section.
